reason: The proposed structures are chemically coherent and their explicit Lean graphs have the claimed connectivity, formulas, neutral valences, and rotational automorphisms. However, the derivation is conditional on a source-unstated restriction of E to a straight-chain C6-symmetric peralkylbenzene family. F and especially G are then produced by specialized, result-shaped graph constructors rather than selected from the full source constraints. The G percentage proof also uses O = 15.999 instead of the supplied periodic-table value O = 16.00. Thus the submission supports the intended structures only under additional disclosed modeling assumptions, not unconditionally from the problem.

coverage.evidence: The explicit graph structureE represents neutral C12H18 hexamethylbenzene; structure_e_connectivity, structure_e_formula, structure_e_valid, and structure_e_has_sixfold_axis verify its atoms, aromatic ring, six methyl groups, valence, and order-6 automorphism. With the supplied C = 12.01 and H = 1.008, its hydrogen content is 11.1817778%, compatible with 11.18%. The theorem nevertheless proves uniqueness only after assuming the candidate-defined symmetricPeralkylbenzene k family, which is not implied by a sixfold axis.

structureF explicitly contains a benzene ring bearing six ring-C(=O)-O-H groups, with formula C12H6O12 and neutral closed-shell valences, as checked by structure_f_connectivity, structure_f_formula, structure_f_valid, and structure_f_has_sixfold_axis. Historical chemical literature independently supports oxidation of hexamethylbenzene to mellitic acid ([Friedel, 1880](https://www.persee.fr/doc/bulmi_0150-9640_1880_num_3_7_2864)). Coverage remains conditional because the theorem inherits the unsupported E-family restriction and defines the specialized oxidation product rather than deriving that reaction model from formal premises.

structureG explicitly represents mellitic trianhydride: six carbonyl carbons remain ring-bound and three oxygens bridge adjacent pairs (0,1), (2,3), and (4,5). structure_g_connectivity, structure_g_formula, structure_g_valid, structure_g_has_threefold_axis, and triple_dehydration_formula_balance verify C12O9, neutral valence, an order-3 graph automorphism, and loss of 3 H2O. Using source masses C = 12.01 and O = 16.00 gives 49.9791753% O, compatible with 49.98%; research identifies this same 1,2:3,4:5,6-trianhydride and approximate D3 structure ([Ermer and Neudörfl, 2000](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/%28SICI%291522-2675%2820000119%2983%3A1%3C300%3A%3AAID-HLCA300%3E3.0.CO%3B2-L)). The Lean equality is conditional because tripleAdjacentDehydration hard-codes the three bridges independently of waters, while structureG is defined as that constructor's output.

unsupported_assumptions: A sixfold molecular axis and 11.18% hydrogen restrict E to hydrocarbons in the candidate-defined unbounded family of benzene rings bearing six identical straight saturated alkyl chains.

The specialized oxidiseSixBenzylicGroups constructor completely captures the source reaction and excludes other substrates or products; this is encoded as a definition rather than a theorem hypothesis.
P2O5 necessarily produces complete dehydration with the particular adjacent pairing built into tripleAdjacentDehydration; the graph topology is not derived from the numerical and symmetry premises.
The oxygen-percentage formalization uses O = 15.999 even though the supplied periodic table prints O = 16.00.
Graph automorphisms are used as surrogates for physical three-dimensional rotation axes without a geometric molecular model.
source_checks: Read TASK.json first and verified all three listed SHA-256 hashes against theory_problem.pdf, T1_page-2.png, and T1_page-3.png.

Directly inspected T1_page-2.png, T1_page-3.png, the original PDF page 8, and blank student answer sheet page 13; page 13 has three untemplated boxes labelled E, F, and G and no stereochemical template.
Directly inspected the supplied periodic table on PDF page 5: H = 1.008, C = 12.01, and O = 16.00.
Confirmed the source states E: 11.18% H and a sixfold axis; E oxidizes with KMnO4/HNO3 to highly symmetrical acid F; P2O5 converts F to binary G with 49.98% O and a threefold axis.
Recalculated from source masses: C12H18 is 11.1817778435% H and C12O9 is 49.9791753436% O, both within the appropriate half-last-place intervals.
proof_checks: lake env lean IChO2026Problems/problem_icho_2026_t1_a5.lean completed through all declarations and printed the final axiom audits without errors.

The final identified_structures theorem depends only on standard Lean axioms propext and Quot.sound; other reported dependencies are likewise standard, including Classical.choice for one numerical theorem.
A repository-wide Lean-source scan found no sorry, admit, unsafe, custom axiom, or native_decide.

The explicit candidate graphs were checked against their definitions: formulas, charges, radicals, bond orders, stereochemical fields, ordinary valence, and stated automorphisms are internally consistent.

The hypotheses are satisfiable, so the main theorem is not vacuous. Its limitation is instead that its variables range over preselected candidate models and omit the source's unrestricted molecular-identification problem.

For G, oxygen_percentage_selects_three_waters genuinely proves waters = 3 within waters ≤ 3, but the graph equality does not use waters: the triple-anhydride connectivity is already fixed by tripleAdjacentDehydration and structureG.
